angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 649,784 km at 22.38 pc = 0.39 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 44.6848 +/- 0.0228 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 22.38 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.934 +/- 0.029 solar radii from Mallorquín et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HD 63433 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract): 649,784 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.956 +/- 0.022 solar masses from Mallorquín et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HD 63433 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5553 +/- 56 K from Mallorquín et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 63433 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mallorquín et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HD 63433 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hd-63433.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.478, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63433 (pscomppars): spectral type G5 V, from Mallorquín et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63433 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.07 dex, from Mallorquín et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63433 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.1261, from Mallorquín et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63433 (pscomppars): age 0.414 Gyr, from Mallorquín et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63433 (pscomppars): rotation period 6.4 d, from Mallorquín et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 63433 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 7.26 km/s, from Mallorquín et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...671A.163M/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.934 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.983. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
